chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man for whom the time of prayer arrives while traveling, and then he enters his house before praying it. He said: 'He prays it as four [rak'at].' And he said: 'He continues to shorten [the prayer] until he enters his house.'

For this narration is understood to mean that if he enters [his house] and the time is still remaining, full prayer is obligatory upon him. As for after the time has passed, he is not obligated to make up the prayer except according to what was missed by him. And likewise, if he sets out for travel and the time is still remaining, shortening is obligatory upon him. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shortening or completing prayers when entering or leaving home during travel time?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between entering a home during active prayer time versus after its expiration, establishing that the obligation to shorten (qasr) persists until the prayer is performed. Scholars interpret this to mean that the transition from travel to residence status is determined by the timing of entry relative to the prayer window, ensuring the traveler maintains the shortened form unless they complete the prayer while still in transit. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of travel status (hukm al-safar) until the act of worship is fulfilled.
